Records ``(entry_id, value)`` pairs such that every id is applied at most
once: re-applying an id that was already applied has no effect.
"""


class Journal:
    """Journal of entries accepted at most once each, keyed by entry id."""

    def __init__(self):
        # entry id -> accepted value (only ids for which apply returned True)
        self._values = {}
        self._total = 0

    def apply(self, entry_id: str, value: int) -> bool:
        """Record ``value`` under ``entry_id``.

        Returns ``True`` if the entry was newly recorded, or ``False`` if
        ``entry_id`` has already been applied (no effect in that case).

        Raises ``ValueError`` if ``entry_id`` is not a non-empty string
        containing at least one non-whitespace character, or if ``value``
        is not an ``int`` (``bool`` is rejected).
        """
        if not isinstance(entry_id, str) or not entry_id.strip():
            raise ValueError(

            )
        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
            raise ValueError("value must be an int (bool is not accepted)")
        if entry_id in self._values:
            return False
        self._values[entry_id] = value
        self._total += value
        return True

    def total(self) -> int:
        """Sum of the values of all accepted entries."""
        return self._total

    def count(self) -> int:
        """Number of accepted entries."""
        return len(self._values)
